01

Exterior & Foundation

Not seen

We walk the perimeter first: where soil meets siding, where downspouts dump, where mulch touches the foundation. A flashlight and a probe tell us what the eye misses.

Checked: grade slope · mulch depth · wood-to-soil · vent screens · downspout extensions

Termites or flying ants?

Three quick checks. Tap what matches what you saw.

Book an inspection

Every inspection ends with a written report: what we saw, what we did not, and what conditions invite termites in.

02

Mud Tubes & Crawlspace Moisture

Conducive

Mud tubes are shelter highways termites build from soil to wood. We break one open to see if it is active, then probe the wood behind it for galleries. In the crawlspace we check for standing water, wood touching soil, blocked vents, and musty air.

Checked: foundation face · piers · foundation wood · vapor barrier · standing water · vent flow

Does your crawlspace invite termites?

Have us look under the house
04

Foundation Wood & Attic

Seen

The foundation wood is where the house sits on its foundation. It is the first piece of wood termites reach from the soil, and the first place we probe. We also check the attic for roof rats, disturbed insulation, and plumbing penetrations.

Checked: foundation wood · band board · rim joist · roof sheathing · eave vents · pipe collars

Liquid or bait: which fits your house?

Liquid treatment

A treated band trenched and rodded around the foundation. Works as a continuous barrier between soil and wood.
